title: kopitiam-ai: replace Qwen default with a curated local model ladder
description:
Maintainer directive (2026-07-25): pivot kopitiam-ai's local-first default away from Qwen to a curated model ladder. Qwen is NOT used by default anymore; it is only loaded if the USER supplies a GGUF.

Proposed ladder (all open-weight, coding/agentic focus):
- Local / small (1B, on-device, weak CPU): MiniCPM5-1B (openbmb) — 1.08B LlamaForCausalLM, Apache-2.0, 128K ctx, GGUF available. https://huggingface.co/openbmb/MiniCPM5-1B
  - Alt 1B candidate: Maincoder-1B (Maincode). https://huggingface.co/Maincode/Maincoder-1B
- Higher range (~3B): stable-code:3b (Stability AI StableCode). https://ollama.com/library/stable-code:3b
- Stronger CPUs: North-mini-code (CohereLabs) — 30B MoE / 3B active, Apache-2.0, agentic coding, 128K ctx, BF16+FP8 (no GGUF noted yet). https://huggingface.co/blog/CohereLabs/introducing-north-mini-code
- Qwen: opt-in only, when the user supplies a GGUF.

Impact / open questions:
- Existing local stack (kopitiam-tensor/runtime/loader/tokenizer) targets Qwen2 + Llama dense arch. MiniCPM5-1B is LlamaForCausalLM (fits). North-mini-code is MoE (NOT supported by the dense loader — needs work) and has no GGUF yet.
- Requires an AID (supersedes/updates AID-0029 adapter selection, and the Qwen assumptions in kopitiam-ai crate docs + docs/SESSION-STATE.md).
- Decide selection policy: default seed model, capability/CPU-based tier selection, user-GGUF override path.

Captured per AGENTS.md (maintainer prompt -> bead, not acted on live). Not yet implemented.

notes.content: License filter: drop stable-code:3b (Stability AI) from the ladder — its community/non-commercial license is incompatible with KOPITIAM's AGPLv3. The ~3B 'higher range' tier is now open (needs an Apache-2.0/MIT/compatible ~3B coder). All remaining ladder models must be OSI-compatible with AGPLv3; MiniCPM5-1B, Maincoder-1B, North-mini-code are Apache-2.0.
notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454

notes.content: PREFERRED on-device default: google/gemma-4-E2B. ~2.3B effective params (5.1B w/ embeddings), multimodal (text+image, audio), coding/reasoning, 128K ctx, GGUF available. LICENSE: Apache-2.0 per authoritative license page (ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/gemma_4_license shows standard Apache-2.0 text, OSI-approved) — AGPLv3-compatible. Gemma 4 moved OFF the old custom 'Gemma Terms of Use'. CAVEAT: card links a separate 'Prohibited use'/'Intended use' policy; core grant is Apache-2.0 but verify that policy is advisory, not incorporated into the license, before shipping. This fills the ~3B tier vacated by stable-code. ENGINEERING IMPACT: Gemma arch (hybrid local/global sliding-window attention + Per-Layer Embeddings) is NOT the current dense Qwen2/Llama loader — needs loader work like North-mini-code; and multimodal is scope beyond the text-only runtime (text-only path first). https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-E2B
notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454

notes.content:
LICENSE SPLIT (authoritative, ai.google.dev/gemma/terms): the Gemma family is NOT uniformly GPLv3-compatible.
- Gemma 4: Apache-2.0 (OSI) → AGPLv3-compatible → OK to make default + BUNDLE/redistribute with kopitiam.
- Gemma 1/2/3/3n + others: 'Gemma Terms of Use' custom license, NOT OSI. Section 3.2 + Prohibited Use Policy: 'You must include the use restrictions ... as an enforceable provision in any agreement governing the use and/or distribution.' Passing restrictions downstream violates GPLv3/AGPLv3 §7 (no further restrictions) → INCOMPATIBLE. kopitiam must NOT bundle or default to these; they may only be USER-SUPPLIED GGUF (same opt-in path as Qwen), where kopitiam never distributes the weights.
RECOMMENDATION: default = Gemma 4 family only (gemma-4-E2B on-device; larger Gemma-4 variants for stronger CPUs). Older Gemma + Qwen = user-supplied-GGUF only. Maincoder-1B/MiniCPM5-1B/North-mini-code (all Apache-2.0) remain compatible bundleable alternatives.
notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454

notes.content: DECISION CONFIRMED by maintainer (2026-07-25): default local family = Gemma 4 (Apache-2.0), bundled — gemma-4-E2B on-device, larger gemma-4-* for stronger CPUs. Pre-4 Gemma (1/2/3/3n) and Qwen are USER-SUPPLIED GGUF ONLY, never bundled/redistributed. North-mini-code / MiniCPM5-1B / Maincoder-1B remain Apache-2.0 bundleable alternatives. stable-code rejected (license). Scope for implementation is now fixed; ready for an AID.
notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454

notes.content: gemma3n:e4b considered: rejected as BUNDLED/DEFAULT on two grounds. (1) License: Gemma 3n is pre-4 → Gemma Terms of Use (not OSI, AGPLv3-incompatible) → user-supplied-GGUF only, per confirmed scope. (2) Not lighter: E4B is ~4B effective vs gemma-4-E2B ~2.3B effective, so the Apache-2.0 default is already lighter. Outcome: gemma-3n (e2b/e4b) available only via the user-GGUF path; default stays gemma-4-E2B.
notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454

notes.content: Runtime loader constraints that shape the Gemma work: (a) K-quant support (Q4_K/Q6_K) is MISSING in kopitiam-loader (only classic quants + F16/BF16). (b) tokenizer path only accepts gpt2 byte-BPE, not SentencePiece — Gemma uses SPM. (c) gemma-4-E2B-it has no GGUF (safetensors only). So 'make Gemma chat' = arch support + SPM tokenizer support + (K-quant or safetensors) loading — three real pieces, not just an arch branch. Track as sub-work under this bead.
notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454

title: kopitiam-ai: gate LocalAdapter::load on general.architecture — fail loud, not garbage
description:
TODAY THERE IS NO ARCHITECTURE GATE. crates/kopitiam-ai/src/local/adapter.rs:126 reads `general.architecture` from the GGUF ONLY to pick a tokenizer (`.or_else(|| loaded.metadata().architecture.clone())`). Nothing anywhere refuses a GGUF whose architecture the runtime cannot actually execute.

kopitiam-runtime implements exactly ONE forward pass — QwenConfig/QwenModel (pre-norm residual, RoPE, grouped-query attention, SwiGLU MLP). Point KOPITIAM_MODEL_GGUF at a Gemma / Phi / Mistral-shaped GGUF and the loader may well parse the tensors, build a QwenModel over them, and start generating — producing NONSENSE rather than an error. Silent wrongness is worse than a crash: the user sees the TUI stream confident garbage with no hint the weights were never runnable.

WHAT TO DO: after kopitiam-loader hands back metadata, check `general.architecture` against a whitelist of what the runtime genuinely implements (today: qwen2, and llama insofar as it is the same dense shape — CONFIRM the llama path is actually exercised before whitelisting it, don't assume). Unknown/unsupported architecture => a clean Err from LocalAdapter::load. adapter.rs's select_adapter already turns a load Err into FallbackReason::LoadFailed with a Singlish note, so the whole degradation path exists — this just needs to reach it.

WHY THIS IS THE FIRST GEMMA BEAD: it is small, independent of every other item under bd-250, and it converts the Gemma failure mode from 'quietly wrong' to 'clearly told'. Worth doing even if the Gemma forward pass never lands.

WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS WRONG: if a whitelist is too tight it locks out GGUFs that DO run fine today (some llama-family quants are dense-Qwen-shaped in every way that matters). Gate on 'can the runtime build a model from this', not on brand names — and test with the two GGUFs already in ~/.cache/kopitiam/models (qwen2.5-0.5b, llama-3.2-1b) to be sure neither regresses to Echo.

Found while answering 'how to run kopitiam tui with gemma' (2026-07-25).

notes.content:
CORRECTION + SHARPENING (verified against the tree on 2026-07-25, not taken from another bead's notes):

My original framing — 'a Gemma GGUF may well load clean and emit garbage' — was OVERSTATED at the time of writing, and is becoming TRUE as the accidental backstops come down. The accurate picture:

TWO GATES were incidentally catching non-Qwen models. Neither was designed as an architecture check.
- QUANT GATE: GONE. bd-uij's comment records gguf.rs mapping only F32/F16/Q4_0/Q4_1/Q5_0/Q5_1/Q8_0/BF16, so K-quant files hard-failed at parse. That is NO LONGER TRUE in the working tree — dtype_from_ggml_type now maps ids 10-15 to Q2_K..Q8_K (the bd-3t0 K-quant work). Modern K-quant GGUFs parse today.
- TOKENIZER GATE: still standing. kopitiam-runtime/src/gguf_tokenizer.rs accepts `tokenizer.ggml.model == "gpt2"` only. Most Gemma GGUFs are SentencePiece, so they still fail here — loudly, which is the correct outcome, but by accident rather than by design.

THE TIMING POINT, AND WHY THIS BEAD IS URGENT: bd-v3x item 2 is 'add SentencePiece tokenizer support'. The moment that lands, the LAST accidental guard is gone — and a Gemma GGUF will parse, tokenize, load into QwenModel, and generate confident nonsense with nothing left to stop it. THIS GATE MUST LAND BEFORE OR TOGETHER WITH THE SPM TOKENIZER WORK, not after. Sequenced any later and there is a window where the product silently lies.

OPEN QUESTION WORTH ANSWERING WHILE BUILDING THIS (a claim I am NOT making, only flagging): llama-3.2-1b-instruct-q4_0 is in the shipped catalog and sitting in ~/.cache/kopitiam/models, and it is gpt2-BPE + Q4_0, so it presumably loads and runs through QwenModel TODAY. But Qwen2 and Llama are not the same dense architecture — Qwen2 carries QKV biases, Llama does not. Either bridge.rs handles that difference correctly, or the second catalog model has been producing subtly wrong output all along. Someone should establish which, with a reference comparison, before the whitelist is written — because the answer decides whether 'llama' belongs on it.

title: kopitiam-runtime: Gemma 4 forward pass (hybrid local/global sliding-window attention + Per-Layer Embeddings)
description:
THE BIG ONE under bd-250. Without this, nothing else makes Gemma runnable.

CURRENT STATE: crates/kopitiam-runtime is a single-architecture engine. config.rs's own doc says it 'encodes one specific architecture family: pre-norm residual', and FORMAT = "qwen-config". The model type is QwenModel: embedding, RoPE, grouped-query attention, SwiGLU MLP, KV cache, greedy sampling. That is Qwen2 (and dense-Llama by coincidence of shape).

GEMMA 4 IS NOT THAT SHAPE. Per bd-250's own engineering note: hybrid local/global sliding-window attention plus Per-Layer Embeddings. Beyond that, the Gemma line historically differs from Qwen in ways that silently corrupt output if you skip them — GeGLU rather than SwiGLU, RMSNorm weights applied as (1 + w), input embeddings scaled by sqrt(d_model), and on Gemma 2/3 logit softcapping and alternating sliding-window layers. VERIFY EACH OF THESE AGAINST GEMMA 4 SPECIFICALLY before implementing; do not port assumptions from Gemma 2/3 blog posts, and do not trust this bead's list as authoritative — it is a starting checklist, not a spec.

ARCHITECTURAL QUESTION TO SETTLE FIRST (this is the real design work, not the kernels): does the runtime grow a second concrete model type, or does it gain a trait that both Qwen and Gemma implement? Today QwenConfig/QwenModel are named concretely throughout, and kopitiam-ai's LocalAdapter is written against them. A second copy-pasted transformer is the tempting-and-wrong answer. Per CLAUDE.md, propose the architecture and record an ADR/AID BEFORE writing the forward pass.

PROVENANCE IS MANDATORY HERE. Per CLAUDE.md's Provenance Standards and the attribution rule: state in rustdoc AT THE POINT OF USE where each layout/algorithm came from (paper, model card, or a specific reference implementation and its license), and distinguish clean-room study from close adaptation. A transformer variant is exactly the kind of hard-won format knowledge that must live next to the code.

SCOPE: text-only path first. Gemma 4 E2B is multimodal (text+image+audio) and that is well beyond the text-only runtime — explicitly out of scope here.

VALIDATION: needs a real gemma-4-E2B GGUF and a known-good reference output to compare against. Greedy decoding with a fixed prompt against llama.cpp's output for the same file is the honest check; 'it emits plausible English' proves nothing, since a wrong forward pass does that too.

DEPENDS ON: nothing in this tree, but pairs with the architecture-gate bead (which stops a Gemma GGUF from silently mis-running before this exists).
closed_reason: Duplicate of bd-v3x, which covers the Gemma forward pass in more depth (arch specifics confirmed against the model card, SentencePiece tokenizer, weights source, plus the maintainer's RAM-gated selection policy). The three genuinely new points — the trait-vs-second-model-type design question, the llama.cpp token-for-token validation method, and the text-only scope fence — have been added to bd-v3x as a comment. Filed before checking existing beads; my mistake.

title: kopitiam-ai: chat template is ChatML-only — dispatch per architecture, add Gemma's <start_of_turn>
description:
crates/kopitiam-ai/src/local/chat_template.rs renders ONE format and only one: ChatML. IM_START = "<|im_start|>", IM_END = "<|im_end|>", and render_chatml() emits a block per message plus an unconditional trailing `<|im_start|>assistant\n` generation prompt. That is Qwen's format, hard-coded — there is no dispatch, no per-model branch, nothing reads the architecture.

Gemma wants a different wire format entirely: `<start_of_turn>user\n{content}<end_of_turn>\n<start_of_turn>model\n`. Note it is 'model', NOT 'assistant', and Gemma has historically had no separate system role — the system prompt gets folded into the first user turn. CONFIRM BOTH AGAINST THE GEMMA 4 MODEL CARD before coding; do not carry these over from Gemma 2 by assumption.

WHY THIS MATTERS EVEN WITH A CORRECT FORWARD PASS: a right model fed the wrong turn markers does not error, it just answers badly — the tokens are in-vocabulary, so nothing crashes. This is the same class of silent wrongness as the missing architecture gate, and it is invisible in a demo where the reply merely looks a bit off.

WHAT TO BUILD: a template selector driven by the GGUF's architecture (and ideally by `tokenizer.chat_template` in the GGUF metadata when present, which is the model's OWN answer and beats any table we hand-maintain). Keep render_chatml() as one implementation behind it, unchanged and still exactly tested — its existing tests assert byte-exact output, which is the right standard for every template added.

KEEP THE EXISTING RIGOUR: chat_template.rs's tests pin exact strings including edge cases (empty history, system-only, no escaping of user content that happens to contain `<|im_end|>`). Any Gemma template must be tested to the same byte-exact standard, including the 'user content containing a literal turn marker is never reinterpreted' case.

BLOCKED-ISH BY: the Gemma forward-pass bead — a template with no engine to run it is untestable end-to-end. But the template itself, and the dispatch mechanism, can be built and unit-tested independently right now.

title: kopitiam-models: add gemma-4-E2B catalog spec + kill the placeholder sha256s that break every pull
description:
TWO PROBLEMS, ONE FILE (crates/kopitiam-models/src/catalog.rs).

(1) NO GEMMA IN THE CATALOG. Catalog::builtin returns exactly two specs: qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct-q4_0 (Apache-2.0) and llama-3.2-1b-instruct-q4_0 (Llama-3.2-Community). `Architecture::Gemma` exists as a bare enum variant at catalog.rs:34-35 with NO spec behind it, so `KOPITIAM_MODEL=gemma-...` does not error — apps/cli/src/adapter.rs's Catalog::find falls back to the default spec, and the user silently gets Qwen while believing they asked for Gemma. Needs a real gemma-4-E2B ModelSpec: id, display_name, Architecture::Gemma, license, artifact url + REAL sha256 + size.

(2) EVERY PULL IS BROKEN BY DESIGN. Both existing entries carry `sha256: PLACEHOLDER_SHA256` (64 zeros) with a `// TODO: record real sha256 after first successful pull`. `kopitiam models pull` therefore downloads hundreds of MB and then DELIBERATELY fails the checksum gate. apps/cli/src/adapter.rs's module docs already call this out as the reason it never calls ensure_available. Both URLs also carry TODO(verify-url) notes saying the exact quant filename is unconfirmed. Net effect: the autofetch path has never actually worked end-to-end, and bring-your-own is the only real route to weights today.

The two GGUFs sitting in ~/.cache/kopitiam/models (qwen2.5-0.5b 409M, llama-3.2-1b 738M) arrived some other way — sha256 them and record the real values, and the existing catalog becomes usable at the same time.

LICENCE GATE — READ bd-250's THIRD COMMENT BEFORE ADDING ANY GEMMA ENTRY. The Gemma family does NOT share one licence. Gemma 4 is Apache-2.0 (OSI) and is therefore compatible with KOPITIAM's GPL-3.0-only, so it may be defaulted to and its URL shipped in the catalog. Gemma 1/2/3/3n are under the custom 'Gemma Terms of Use', whose §3.2 requires passing use-restrictions downstream as an enforceable term — that collides head-on with GPLv3 §7's no-further-restrictions rule. Those must NEVER be added to the built-in catalog; they are user-supplied-GGUF only, via KOPITIAM_MODEL_GGUF, where KOPITIAM never distributes the weights. The `license` field on the spec is not decoration — it is the record of that decision, so fill it exactly.

ALSO VERIFY (bd-250 comment 2 flagged it unresolved): Gemma 4's card links a separate Prohibited Use / Intended Use policy. Confirm that policy is ADVISORY and not incorporated into the Apache-2.0 grant before shipping a bundled default. If it turns out to be incorporated, Gemma 4 drops to user-supplied-only with the older Gemmas and this bead's premise collapses — say so in an AID rather than quietly shipping it.

NOTE the crate already has a mechanism for this: catalog.rs's own comment points at kopitiam-56q for building specs from HF repo/filename/sha with a pinned commit revision, and src/hf.rs exists. Prefer that over hand-writing a third entry.
closed_reason: Duplicate of bd-uij, which already covers the gemma-4 catalog entry, the placeholder-sha256 gate, and the need for real pinned HF coordinates. The one new point (Catalog::find silently substitutes the default spec for an unknown model id, so KOPITIAM_MODEL=gemma-... quietly returns Qwen) has been added to bd-uij as a comment. Filed before checking existing beads; my mistake.

title: kopitiam-loader/tensor: GGUF K-quant dequant (Q4_K/Q5_K/Q6_K/…), bit-exact
description: Add K-quant dequantization so modern GGUFs (Q4_K_M etc.) load. Bit-exact to ggml. Reference: vendored crates/kopitiam-ai/vendor/llama.cpp (ggml-quants.c, ggml-common.h), MIT, attributed at point of use. Wires new DType variants (kopitiam-core) + dtype_from_ggml_type (loader) + dequant (tensor) + bridge (runtime). In progress via agent. Unblocks loading modern quants; prerequisite context for the Gemma demo (bd for gemma arch/tokenizer). See bd-uij loader-reality notes.

title: kvim publish tree still AGPL-3.0-only on crates.io — needs 0.1.8 relicense bump
description:
Repo relicensed AGPL-3.0-only -> GPL-3.0-only in 213e619 (2026-07-25 07:24 SGT), but all 7 crates in the kvim publish tree are live on crates.io at 0.1.7 with `license = "AGPL-3.0-only"`: kopitiam-ontology, kopitiam-config, kopitiam-syntax, kopitiam-snippet, kopitiam-lua, kopitiam-semantic, kopitiam-neovim (all published 2026-07-18).

crates.io versions are immutable — cannot patch metadata in place. Only fix is bump [workspace.package].version 0.1.7 -> 0.1.8 and re-run scripts/publish-kvim.sh.

Verified by diffing the published .crate against the working tree: kopitiam-neovim 0.1.7 source is otherwise IDENTICAL to local — only src/icons.rs (one rustdoc line, AGPLv3->GPLv3) and README.md (two lines) differ. So this is a licence-metadata-only republish, no feature/bugfix content.

Blast radius: workspace version is shared, so the bump also moves the CLI publish tree (scripts/publish.sh) — those crates are equally AGPL-stale on crates.io. kopitiam-core/kopitiam-tensor are on their own 0.0.x line and unaffected by the kvim tree.

PUBLISH IS MAINTAINER-GATED — agent must not run publish-kvim.sh.

title: OpenFOAM → KOPITIAM scientific crates: FVM/solver translation roadmap
description: 3-part OpenFOAM-dev survey (GPL-3.0 vendored, future work). Translate FV math+data-layout, not C++ machinery. Crates to build: kopitiam-units (Dimension[i8;7]+Dimensioned<T>), NEW kopitiam-mesh (polyMesh: points+CSR faces+owner/neighbour, geometry algos, ASCII reader), kopitiam-discretization (Field<T,Loc>, fvc:: Gauss ops, enum schemes), kopitiam-equation (FvMatrix LDU + fvm::), kopitiam-solver (LduMatrix+PCG/PBiCGStab+DIC/DILU, defer GAMG), kopitiam-scientific (ODE: ButcherTableau RK). First targets: Dimension → mesh geom+owner/neighbour → Field → fvc grad/laplacian → FvMatrix LDU + PCG; milestone = steady diffusion solve with analytic test. Decisions: add mesh/solver/scientific crates; runtime Dimension vs uom; fields no-mesh-ref; enum-dispatch schemes; serial-first keep MPI out of v1; translate-vs-reimplement-from-literature per item. Full detail in session notes; recommend ADR + engineering-journal before coding.

title: Unblock the crates.io publish chain: tensor/models 0.0.2 bump, kopitiam-ai vendor exclude, apps/cli path dep
description:
scripts/publish.sh now covers all 17 crates `kopitiam` (apps/cli) depends on, in topological order, with per-crate versions (the workspace is no longer single-version). Its preflight blocks the run on four things. One is done, three are NOT — they sit in files owned by other agents this session, so this session never touched them.

DONE (this session):
- kopitiam-core 0.0.1 -> 0.0.2 (crates/kopitiam-core/Cargo.toml) + matching req in root Cargo.toml [workspace.dependencies]. Workspace resolves; Cargo.lock updated.
- scripts/publish.sh: 9 -> 17 crates, per-crate crate_version(), preflight, quiet already_published().

STILL BLOCKING (preflight FATALs, in order):
1. kopitiam-tensor is live at 0.0.1 but its local source has moved on — published dtype.rs has no Q2_K..Q8_K, local quant.rs/storage.rs/tensor/{concat,matmul}.rs all use them. Bump to 0.0.2 in crates/kopitiam-tensor/Cargo.toml AND the req in root Cargo.toml, same commit. ^0.0.1 matches ONLY 0.0.1 (every 0.0.x is its own major), so bumping one side alone breaks the local build.
2. kopitiam-models same story: live at 0.0.1, local has a new src/hf.rs plus changed catalog.rs/lib.rs. Needs 0.0.2. It is pinned inline in its own [package], no workspace req to chase.
3. crates/kopitiam-ai/Cargo.toml needs `exclude = ["vendor/"]`. .gitignore does not save you — vendor/llama.cpp is a nested git repo and cargo's packager walks in. Measured: cargo package --list -p kopitiam-ai = 677 files, 660 under vendor/, ~198 MB vs crates.io's 10 MiB cap. Also a GPLv3 hygiene problem: do not ship vendored llama.cpp/ggml/candle/tensorflow inside our tarball.
4. apps/cli/Cargo.toml line 24: kopitiam-models = { path = "../../crates/kopitiam-models" } has no version, so `kopitiam` itself cannot publish. Move it to root [workspace.dependencies] with path+version and use { workspace = true } here, like every other internal dep.

ALSO WORTH DOING BEFORE ANY PUBLISH (not preflight-enforced):
- No crate dir carries a LICENSE file. cargo only packages files under the crate dir, so the root LICENSE never travels — every published tarball so far ships GPL-3.0-only with no licence text in it. kopitiam-core 0.0.1 already went up that way.
- kopitiam-ai (and most of the runtime chain) has no README, so the crates.io page renders blank. Ties into the CLAUDE.md open question about Singlish on docs.rs / the public crate face.

RATE LIMIT: six brand-new names in the list (loader, tokenizer, runtime, ai, workflow, kopitiam). crates.io burst is 5, refill 1 per 10 min, so expect one ~10 min pause near the end. publish_with_retry() parses the Retry-After and sleeps it out. Bumping an existing name is a looser limit.

Publishing stays maintainer-only: run ./scripts/publish.sh --dry-run first, and the real run only on an explicit prompt.

notes.content:
PROGRESS 2026-07-25 (SGT, Saturday — outside NUS hours):

kopitiam-ai's whole dependency closure is now publish-clean. Verified with
  cargo publish --dry-run --allow-dirty -p kopitiam-core -p kopitiam-tensor -p kopitiam-loader -p kopitiam-tokenizer -p kopitiam-runtime -p kopitiam-ai
all six package + verify, nothing uploaded. Release tests green across the six (28/15/18/12/122/123/43/9 passed, 0 failed).

DONE:
- kopitiam-core 0.0.1 -> 0.0.2, kopitiam-tensor 0.0.1 -> 0.0.2, both with matching reqs in root Cargo.toml [workspace.dependencies] (same commit — ^0.0.x is exact).
- crates/kopitiam-ai/Cargo.toml: exclude = ["vendor/"]. cargo package --list went 677 files / ~198 MB -> 16 files / 94.6 KiB (29.7 KiB compressed). Was a hard crates.io 10 MiB failure AND a GPLv3 hygiene problem.
- .gitignore: crates/kopitiam-ai/vendor/ -> crates/*/vendor/, with a note that gitignore alone does NOT keep a nested-repo vendor tree out of cargo package.
- scripts/publish.sh: 17-crate topological list, per-crate crate_version(), 4-check preflight, quiet already_published() (no more curl 404 spam).

STILL BLOCKING the FULL chain (both about kopitiam-models, which is a dep of apps/cli, NOT of kopitiam-ai — out of scope of the session's instruction, files left untouched):
1. kopitiam-models live at 0.0.1 but local source has a new src/hf.rs + changed catalog.rs/lib.rs. Needs 0.0.2 in crates/kopitiam-models/Cargo.toml (pinned inline, no workspace req to chase).
2. apps/cli/Cargo.toml:24 — kopitiam-models = { path = "../../crates/kopitiam-models" } has no version, so `kopitiam` itself cannot publish. Move to root [workspace.dependencies] with path+version, use { workspace = true } here.

NEW FINDING — publish.sh may be largely obsolete. Cargo 1.97 supports multi-package publish (cargo publish -p a -p b ...): it computes the topological order ITSELF and verifies each package against a temp registry built from its packaged siblings, so a whole chain of never-published interdependent crates can be dry-run in one shot (proved above). That removes the need for the script's hand-rolled CRATES ordering AND wait_for_index(). What stays worth keeping: the preflight checks (stale-seed, vendor/, path-dep-without-version) and publish_with_retry()'s 429 Retry-After handling, none of which cargo does. Worth an AID + a rewrite pass.

NOT DONE, still worth doing before any real publish: no crate dir carries a LICENSE file (cargo only packages files under the crate dir, so root LICENSE never travels — every tarball so far ships GPL-3.0-only with no licence text); no README on the runtime chain, so crates.io pages render blank.

Nothing committed, nothing published.

title: kopitiam tui: auto-download the local model on startup
description:
Maintainer wants the TUI to auto-download the Gemma model when it starts (instead of falling back to Echo when no .gguf is present).

BLOCKERS / prerequisites (why this can't just be switched on):
1. No concrete Gemma catalog entry. kopitiam-models has Family::Gemma enum only; no ModelSpec with repo/commit/filename. Every catalog sha256 is the placeholder 0x64, so ensure_available's checksum gate REJECTS any download until a real sha256 (+ pinned HF commit) is recorded. Need real gemma-4-E2B GGUF coordinates (HF repo, commit SHA, filename, sha256, size).
2. Loader can't run gemma-4 arch yet (see bd-250): hybrid local/global attention + Per-Layer Embeddings not in the dense Qwen2/Llama loader. Downloaded gemma-4 would fail LocalAdapter::load -> Echo. So auto-download of gemma-4 is pointless until loader support lands.
3. Design principle: apps/cli/src/adapter.rs deliberately does NOT autofetch ('rude surprise sia'). Auto-download-on-start must be consented (first-run prompt) + show progress in the TUI, not silent. kopitiam-models::ensure_available + hf.rs give the fetch+verify+progress plumbing to build on.

RECOMMENDED SEQUENCING:
- Build the TUI auto-download mechanism model-agnostically (consent screen + progress bar over ensure_available), pointed at a runnable Apache-2.0 model that WORKS on today's loader as the shipping default (MiniCPM5-1B, Llama arch, GGUF available) — needs its real catalog entry too.
- Land gemma-4 loader support (bd-250), add the real gemma-4-E2B catalog entry, then flip the TUI default to gemma-4.
Depends on bd-250.

notes.content:
LOADER REALITY (from research + code read, applies to any download target):
1. QUANT GATE: kopitiam-loader/src/gguf.rs:241-252 dtype_from_ggml_type only maps F32,F16,Q4_0,Q4_1,Q5_0,Q5_1,Q8_0,BF16. K-quants (Q4_K_M/Q6_K) HARD-FAIL at parse. Most modern small GGUFs are K-quants. Bridge confirms: kopitiam-runtime/src/bridge.rs:43 handles only Q4_0|Q4_1|Q5_0|Q5_1|Q8_0.
2. TOKENIZER GATE: kopitiam-runtime/src/gguf_tokenizer.rs expects tokenizer.ggml.model=='gpt2' (byte-level BPE + merges). SentencePiece/llama tokenizers error.
=> Effectively only Qwen-style classic-quant GGUFs actually load+chat today.

gemma-4-E2B-it (https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-E2B-it): Apache-2.0 CONFIRMED, but ships model.safetensors ONLY (NO GGUF), ~5B params (multi-GB). Not llama-shaped, SentencePiece tokenizer => cannot load on current runtime. Downloading it = large pull -> Echo. Do NOT wire the downloader to it yet.

Runnable-today stand-in that stays non-Qwen: MiniCPM5-1B-Q8_0.gguf (openbmb/MiniCPM5-1B-GGUF, Apache-2.0) is a supported quant (Q8_0) — BUT verify its tokenizer.ggml.model=='gpt2' first (MiniCPM base is SPM; if so it fails the tokenizer gate too). Q4_K_M variant is unsupported (K-quant).
notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454

notes.content:
ONE ADDITION from a 2026-07-25 code read (bd-250.4 was filed covering this ground and is closed as a duplicate of this bead; everything else in it — placeholder sha256 gate, need for real HF coordinates, the Gemma licence split — is already captured here or in bd-250's comments):

`KOPITIAM_MODEL=gemma-...` DOES NOT ERROR — IT SILENTLY GIVES YOU QWEN. apps/cli/src/adapter.rs's select_adapter does:

    let spec = Catalog::find(&model_id).unwrap_or_else(|| Catalog::find(DEFAULT_MODEL_ID).expect(...));

So an unknown/unimplemented catalog id falls back to the default spec with NO message. `Architecture::Gemma` exists as a bare enum variant (catalog.rs:34-35) with no ModelSpec behind it, so a user who sets KOPITIAM_MODEL to any Gemma id today gets Qwen2.5-0.5B and is told nothing — SelectedAdapter::notice() reports 'Using local model on CPU: <qwen path>', which is truthful but does not mention that the model they ASKED for was silently discarded.

Small standalone fix, independent of everything else in this bead: an unknown model id should be a clear error (or at minimum a loud note naming both the requested id and the substituted one). The fallback itself is defensible — it keeps the offline path working — but it must be visible. Worth doing NOW, before any auto-download work, because it is the difference between 'Gemma isn't supported yet' and 'Gemma appeared to work'.
notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454

title: kopitiam-runtime: Gemma architecture + SentencePiece tokenizer (make Gemma chat)
description:
Goal: a working Gemma demo in the kopitiam TUI. Requires REAL new runtime work (not a config branch). Sequenced AFTER the K-quant agent releases kopitiam-runtime (one-directory-one-owner).

THREE pieces:
1. Gemma architecture in kopitiam-runtime forward pass. Differs from the current llama/qwen2 dense path: input embedding scaled by sqrt(hidden_size); GeGLU (gelu-gated) MLP not SwiGLU; RMSNorm uses (1 + weight); tied input/output embeddings; per-layer alternating local(sliding-window)/global attention (gemma-2/3/4); attention logit soft-capping (gemma-2). Confirm gemma-4-E2B specifics from config.json (https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-E2B-it). Reference: vendored llama.cpp ggml + llm_build_gemma (crates/kopitiam-ai/vendor/llama.cpp), MIT, attribute at point of use.
2. SentencePiece tokenizer support. Runtime today only builds a gpt2 byte-BPE tokenizer (kopitiam-runtime/src/gguf_tokenizer.rs expects tokenizer.ggml.model=='gpt2'). Gemma uses SPM (tokenizer.model / tokenizer.json). Need an SPM path (pure-Rust; e.g. parse tokenizer.json unigram/spm, or the GGUF llama/spm vocab).
3. Weights source. gemma-4-E2B-it ships model.safetensors only (no GGUF), ~5B params, Apache-2.0. Loader claims SafeTensors parsing — verify it can feed the Gemma forward pass. OR use a Gemma GGUF if one exists.

DECISION PENDING (gates feasibility/time): demo on gemma-4-E2B-it (safetensors, newest, hardest, likely no GGUF) vs a mature Gemma with existing community GGUFs (gemma-2-2b-it / gemma-3) as the demo vehicle — same arch+tokenizer work, but a real GGUF to load today.

Blocks on: bd-250 (loader/arch constraints). Working Qwen-0.5B demo already proves the TUI end-to-end (interim runnable model).

notes.content: MODEL-SELECTION POLICY (maintainer, 2026-07-25): once Gemma runs, DEFAULT = Gemma (gemma-4-E2B-it), FALLBACK = Qwen-0.5B on devices with < 10 GB total RAM. Implement a RAM-aware tier in select_adapter: read total system RAM; >=10GB -> Gemma, <10GB -> Qwen. 10GB threshold is right because dequant-to-f32 expands gemma-4-E2B (~5B params) to ~f32 in memory (~10GB). SEQUENCING / do-not-regress: keep Qwen the working default NOW; only flip to Gemma-default when this bead's arch+SPM-tokenizer+weights land (else >=10GB machines fall back to Echo and lose today's working Qwen chat). Ship the RAM selector together with Gemma support, not before. Qwen stays as the explicit low-RAM fallback (this supersedes the earlier 'Qwen only if user supplies GGUF' — Qwen is now the bundled low-RAM fallback tier).
notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454

notes.content:
POLICY REFINED (maintainer): Qwen and other Chinese-origin models (MiniCPM/openbmb, etc.) are LAST RESORT, not the fallback tier. Corrected ladder:
- Default (>=10GB RAM): Gemma (gemma-4-E2B-it) — Google, Apache-2.0.
- Low-RAM (<10GB): a LOWER-PARAMETER, license-clean (GPL-3.0-compatible: Apache-2.0/MIT), NON-Chinese model. Candidates to evaluate: smaller Gemma variants, SmolLM (HF, Apache-2.0), Phi (Microsoft, MIT) — final pick TBD, must also be loader-compatible.
- LAST RESORT only: Qwen (Alibaba) + other Chinese models.
CAVEAT: today the ONLY runnable model is Qwen (gpt2-BPE tokenizer + qwen2 arch + classic quant). The preferred non-Chinese small models mostly use SentencePiece tokenizers, so they depend on the SAME SPM-tokenizer + arch work as Gemma (this bead). So Qwen remains the INTERIM runnable stopgap until SPM+arch lands, then it demotes to last-resort. Selection stays RAM-gated (>=10GB Gemma / <10GB small non-Chinese).
notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454

notes.content:
ADDITIONS from a 2026-07-25 code read (bd-250.2 was filed covering this same ground and has been closed as a duplicate of this bead — these are the only parts not already here):

1. DESIGN QUESTION TO SETTLE BEFORE ANY KERNELS: does kopitiam-runtime grow a SECOND concrete model type, or a trait both Qwen and Gemma implement? Today QwenConfig/QwenModel are named concretely throughout (config.rs literally sets FORMAT = "qwen-config" and its docs say it 'encodes one specific architecture family'), and kopitiam-ai's LocalAdapter is written against them. A copy-pasted second transformer is the tempting and wrong answer. Per CLAUDE.md, propose the architecture and record an AID BEFORE writing the forward pass — this is the real design work, the kernels are the easy half.

2. VALIDATION METHOD. 'It emits plausible English' proves nothing — a subtly wrong forward pass does exactly that (wrong RMSNorm convention, missing sqrt(hidden_size) embedding scale, SwiGLU where GeGLU belongs). The honest check is greedy decoding with a fixed prompt and fixed seed compared against llama.cpp's output for the SAME GGUF file, token for token. Worth building that comparison harness as part of this bead, not after.

3. SCOPE FENCE: gemma-4-E2B is multimodal (text+image+audio). Text-only path first, explicitly out of scope here — worth stating so it does not creep.
